summary: Slice A2 of 0.8.7 (prompt reuse and the memory sum) is built in the worktree. It is not committed and is saved as a patch. The memory sum lives in resource_control (memory_shape, memory_sum, reuse_ladder) and reads the GGUF metadata that gguf_inspect gives. Hybrid models get exact terms: KV on the attention layers only, one recurrent state, the checkpoints and the RAM prompt cache. A dense model's estimate is unchanged to the byte. local_brain.configuration takes the first reuse rung the one rule admits, in this order: six checkpoints with a 512 MiB cache (small model) or 1,024 MiB cache (large model); then two checkpoints with 256 MiB; then reuse off, which is today's launch. Every term is counted. The launch line is local_brain.launch_arguments, which matches the golden list: --parallel 1, --cache-ram N, --ctx-checkpoints N, --checkpoint-min-step 0, and still --no-slots, --no-cache-idle-slots and --offline. It never carries --slot-save-path. completion sends cache_prompt true. The new workbench/brain_briefs.py keeps one brief per kind. Each brief is primed once after Ready with no answer (max_tokens 0, laid out as [brief, a fixed line]). The kept prefix is tracked per worker in the brain.kept setting, which holds digests and counts only. A watchdog compares cache_n with the expected kept prefix: two misses in a row re-prime that kind in the background, and the miss is counted on the brain.turn/1 record under 'reuse'. Forget marks the live worker that may hold the forgotten turn. From then on, turns.ask sends it nothing (NOT_SENT, FORGETTING), and when the caller may restart a model, local_brain.forget_restart queues a brain.activate of the same selection. That job runs once the worker is idle; the queue and the hold apply. The new worker is primed with briefs only. turns.LocalPort now reports kept tokens, so questions are priced and capped on new tokens. The smoke script printed 18 of 18 OK on a throwaway copy. One real 4B run, under the model lock on a quiet machine (load 0.24), went through Graphite's own sealed start with the new launch line: the first question after priming reused its kept brief (cache_n 1006, 83 tokens new, 2.22 s), and the second question of the same kind reused messages 1 to 3 (cache_n 1069, 21 tokens new, 0.94 s). Nothing was tested in the owner's sense, and nothing ran on the owner's ThinkPad.

The brain.kept row holds no canary, and the stored turn is a tombstone.

Activation took 9.2 s, the seal was SEALED, and the worker came up with reuse {checkpoints 6, prompt_cache_mb 512}, 39 launch arguments and a 4,774 MiB estimate. Priming read the stand-in kind's 1,009-token brief in 14.3 s (prompt_n 1022, no answer). Questions of that kind over five invented Rail Demo and Home Demo things, as cache_n / prompt_n / seconds: (1) 'which is the newer bench supply': 1006 / 83 / 2.22 s, answer 1. (2) 'and the deposit clause of the lease': 1069 / 21 / 0.94 s, answer 3. (3) 'the older datasheet': 1069 / 18 / 0.94 s, answer 2. (4) the list reversed (a different message 2): 1006 / 80 / 2.30 s, answer 1. Each cache_n was 3 short of the expected kept prefix (1009, then 1072), inside the watchdog's tolerance of 4, so there were no misses. Readback: resident 4,024 MB against the 5,006 MB estimate, no flag. At the runtime's default verbosity no checkpoint size was logged, so it shows as NOT_LOGGED. The model was stopped at the end, and no llama-server is left running.

sockets: No 0.8.6 socket is needed by A2; it is engine-only, in lane A. No guarded import of a 0.8.6 module was written.

Priming primes whatever kinds turns.discover() finds. In this tree no module registers a kind at import (lanes B and C have not merged), so after a real activation 'kept_briefs.primed' is []. Lanes B and C's kinds will be primed with no further change once they register at import.

The brain.turn.forget operation (approve scope, always asked) is A4's. turns.forget(kernel, owner, id, principal) already marks the worker and queues the restart when given a principal that may restart a model. Without one, the worker stays marked: turns are not sent to it until it is restarted or stopped, and brain.status shows kept_briefs.forget_pending.
brain_clock.py (A3) is still a guarded import in turns. FixedClock now prices on new tokens, because kept() is real.
decisions: The reuse ladder has a third rung, reuse off, beyond the design's two (6 checkpoints with 512 or 1,024 MiB, then 2 with 256). Reason: without it, the 35B would be refused at availabilities where it is admitted today (32,140 to 32,521 MiB). With it, the A2 example 'admitted within 200 MiB of 32,157' holds: the lowest admission is 32,140.
The cache size is 1,024 MiB when the weights exceed 8 GiB and 512 MiB otherwise. This reproduces the design's '512 on the 4B here; 1,024 on the 35B'; the design gives no rule for models in between.

Dense models keep today's estimate and launch exactly (--cache-ram 0, --ctx-checkpoints 0). Their prefix is kept by the slot's own KV with cache_prompt, so nothing is added, which is what 'a dense model's estimate unchanged' requires. --checkpoint-min-step 0 is on every launch line (harmless at 0 checkpoints) so the golden list has one shape.
Hybrid terms use integer arithmetic (weights x13 // 10, rounded up). The dense estimate keeps its original float expression so it stays byte-identical.
A hybrid model whose metadata lacks one of the SSM terms is refused (MODEL_MEMORY_ESTIMATE_UNAVAILABLE) rather than estimated as dense.

Priming lays out [brief, a fixed user line] with max_tokens 0. The runtime checkpoints at the start of the last user message, which is the end of the brief, so a question whose message 2 differs still reuses the brief (seen in the real run: 1006 kept on a reversed list). The expected kept prefix is measured with the worker's own template and tokenizer as the shared prefix of two renderings. That was 3 tokens above the real cache_n every time, and the tolerance is 4.

A watchdog 'miss' is cache_n more than 4 short of the expected kept prefix. The expectation is messages 1 to 3 when they were the last asked of the kind, otherwise the primed brief, otherwise 0, in which case nothing is counted. After two misses, re-priming runs on one background thread (one read at a time). Misses go only into the turn record's 'reuse' and the brain.kept counts, never into errors.

Forget restarts through a brain.activate job of the same selection (built like brain.restore), not by a direct kill and start. That way the inference lane waits for running model work ('once idle'), a hold holds it, admission counts memory, and run_model_job's sequential handover and priming are reused. Until the restart, the marked worker gets no turns, so nothing it remembers is used. A worker started after the turn was asked is not restarted (NOTHING_HELD).
The kept-brief store's worker identity includes the worker's 'started' time, so a restart always starts an empty store.

After every load (and after priming) a readback is stored in brain.kept: resident memory against the estimate, and the logged checkpoint size against one state when the runtime logs it. A term off by more than 10 % is flagged. Nothing changes the rule by itself.
No operation, schema or setting was added, so the registry record was not regenerated. tools/record_registry.py --check on a copy reported 'differences: []'.
Talk and App plans (slate_stream, run_reply) keep their own reuse logic unchanged. Only turns' completion and the ready probe now send cache_prompt true.
not_done: The reuse bench (200 questions), I05 and the 35B's checkpoint and cache sizes are for the ThinkPad and the test pass before 0.8.8. Only one short 4B run was done here.
The Brain room (brain_qt) does not yet show the kept-brief line or misses. brain.status carries them in 'kept_briefs' and worker 'reuse' and 'memory_sum'.

The checkpoint size could not be read back from the runtime's log at its default verbosity, and verbose logs are forbidden by the seal. The readback says NOT_LOGGED; the model check (A5) should measure it another way, for example from resident growth.
Whether checkpoints and the RAM cache sit in GPU or host memory on Vulkan was not tried (no GPU here). The budget counts them either way.
The forget restart via a real brain.activate job was not run end to end with a real model. Its job submission was captured in the smoke, and the restart itself was simulated on the fake server.
No test files were written. The test suite, the tiers, the R campaign and the window checks were not run (the owner's rule). Nothing ran on the owner's ThinkPad.
release_note: Kas now keeps each kind of question's standing brief ready in her model's memory, so a second question of the same kind reads only what is new: on the 4B here, 21 new tokens and under a second instead of the whole 1,000-token brief. Her model's memory is now counted exactly for models like the 35B, including what it keeps ready. Forgetting something makes her restart the model once it is idle, so nothing forgotten stays in it.
